<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אלול_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518920487_theRebbe_9" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_9C_D7_95_D7_9C_meluket__BH_POST_1766518920487_theRebbe_9__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the opening header and date for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Night of the third [day] of Selichos,</t>
    <t s="2">the year 5720*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the two interpretations of "seek My face" in prayer, corresponding to supplication and searching, which are the heart's work within and with the heart.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"To You my heart said: 'Seek My face' etc."1,</t>
    <t s="1">And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, brings in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh"2</t>
    <t s="2">Rashi's commentary on the verse,</t>
    <t s="3">that there are two interpretations in "Lecha" [to you/for you].</t>
    <t s="4">For you, in your mission, and in your place.</t>
    <t s="5">And he continues in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="6">that also in "seek My face" there are two interpretations.</t>
    <t s="7">That "seek" is a request and supplication,</t>
    <t s="8">and that "seek" is a request and search.</t>
    <t s="9">And he explains,</t>
    <t s="10">that these two matters</t>
    <t s="11">(request and supplication,</t>
    <t s="12">request and search)</t>
    <t s="13">are in prayer.</t>
    <t s="14">For prayer is a request and supplication,</t>
    <t s="15">and the request is that he succeed in his service to search and find the ways of correction in all his matters.</t>
    <t s="16">And this is what is written: "To You my heart said: 'Seek My face'"</t>
    <t s="17">(specifically "my heart"),</t>
    <t s="18">because the two matters of "seek My face" are in prayer</t>
    <t s="19">(as above),</t>
    <t s="20">and prayer is the service of the heart3.</t>
    <t s="21">And he adds in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="22">that in the service of the heart there are two matters.</t>
    <t s="23">Within the heart and with the heart.</t>
    <t s="24">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="25">that these two matters correspond to the two interpretations</t>
    <t s="26">(above)</t>
    <t s="27">in "seek My face."</t>
    <t s="28">For the request and supplication in prayer come through the service within the heart,</t>
    <t s="29">so that his request and supplication will be true,</t>
    <t s="30">it is by arousing his heart,</t>
    <t s="31">service in the heart itself.</t>
    <t s="32">And the search in prayer</t>
    <t s="33">(how to correct all his matters)</t>
    <t s="34">is service with the heart.</t>
    <t s="35">That is,</t>
    <t s="36">the service is</t>
    <t s="37">(not in the heart,</t>
    <t s="38">but)</t>
    <t s="39">in all his matters,</t>
    <t s="40">except that this service is through the heart4.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the verse "From my flesh I shall perceive G-d," distinguishing between intellectual and tangible perception, and how human soul-powers derive from the supernal Sefiros.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">And to explain this,</t>
    <t s="2">the maamar prefaces with what is written5</t>
    <t s="3">"And from my flesh I shall perceive G-d,"</t>
    <t s="4">that one must understand: the main thing is the soul, so why does it say "And from my flesh I shall perceive"?</t>
    <t s="5">And he explains,</t>
    <t s="6">that in perception there are two modes,</t>
    <t s="7">intellectual perception and tangible perception.</t>
    <t s="8">For intellectual perception relates more to the soul,</t>
    <t s="9">and tangible perception relates more to the body.</t>
    <t s="10">And this distinction is also regarding the thing perceived.</t>
    <t s="11">For in every thing there is a body and a soul.</t>
    <t s="12">For even in physical things there is the soul within them6,</t>
    <t s="13">and even in spiritual things there is the body within them.</t>
    <t s="14">And therefore it says "And from my flesh I shall perceive G-d,"</t>
    <t s="15">because the intent of "I shall perceive G-d" is for tangible perception in G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="16">for there are matters of G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="17">such as Divine Providence,</t>
    <t s="18">that one can perceive tangibly.</t>
    <t s="19">And he continues in the maamar7</t>
    <t s="20">in the explanation of the verse "And from my flesh I shall perceive G-d,"</t>
    <t s="21">that the powers of the human soul descend from the supernal Sefiros8</t>
    <t s="22">as it is written9</t>
    <t s="23">"Let us make man in our image, after our likeness,"</t>
    <t s="24">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="25">from the powers of the human soul one can understand the supernal Sefiros.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
